one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event sits in the window: Q2 FY27 results on 2026-12-01 after the close [17]. Guide $525-535M; consensus $531.95M revenue and $1.28 EPS [18]; our build $534.5M and ~$1.32 non-GAAP EPS, i.e. a small beat, in line with the last two quarters' +1.6-1.9% beats [4][1] rather than the older +12-20%. The swing is the 2H commentary (optical >$600M, 1.6T AEC timing, Q3 guide vs $643M consensus [18]) and anything on AEC share after the Marvell settlement [15]. After the Q1 beat the stock fell over 50% from mid-August [22], so a beat does not imply a rise. The stock rose ~24% today on a sector rebound [23] after falling to $99.86 on 2026-11-20 [19]; short-term reversal cuts both ways. We center the month at $126 (+1%) with a 29% one-month log spread (100% annual realized vol / 3.5, which already includes earnings-day moves).

fair_value.method: Research target (12m) $174.77 = 60% P/E leg ($148.74: 16.5x horizon NTM adjusted EPS ~$9.0) + 40% FCF-yield leg ($213.80 at 3.0%), on a quarterly AI-capex x capture build: FY27 revenue $2,494M / EPS $6.21, FY28 $3,531M / $8.54 (consensus $3.88B / $9.71).

methods.inputs: horizon NTM adjusted EPS ~$9.0 (our build: FY28 $8.54, FY29 $8.86) x 16.5x; peer median 22.6x shrunk to CRDO's 15.2x with k=0.8

Forecast: Q2 FY27 1.40 (copper ~$474M, consistent with inventory up $62M q/q to $313M and $213M non-cancelable supply commitments [1][2]); then ~-4.5%/quarter to 1.09 by Q4 FY28 as (a) 1.6T AEC competition arrives: Marvell demonstrated 800G/1.6T AECs at SC26 [16] and settled its patent challenges with Credo [15]; MaxLinear's CEO Kishore Seendripu (competitor, not a Credo statement) targets 20-30% of 1.6T cables [19]; Cisco sought quotes for a proprietary 1.6T cable program [20]; (b) the CEO Bill Brennan said 1.6T AEC comes in 'in a much bigger way' in FY28 [13], which offsets part of the share loss; then -1%/quarter in FY29 as share settles. Other evidence-based builds: consensus FY28 revenue $3.88B [18] (copper capture held ~1.25 through FY28, +~$0.4B revenue); share held at ~93-99% (no competitor ramp) = upside case; share falling to ~70% in 1.6T = downside case.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Consensus-like path (capture ~1.25 held) adds ~$0.4B FY28 revenue and ~+$15/share; a fast share loss is the downside case.

inputs_detail.derivation: Optical revenue is not disclosed. FY26 base estimated at $63M (8/12/18/25 by quarter) and Q1 FY27 $35M (record optical DSP plus first PIC revenue per Bill Brennan, CEO [14]); flag: low confidence, it only splits the reported total. Forecast optical revenue = capture x capex: Q2 FY27 0.18 (~$61M), Q3 0.45 (~$170M), Q4 0.70 (~$291M) = FY27 ~$556M, 7% below the CEO's 'more than $600 million' [13] because three new product lines (ZeroFlap, PICs, 1.6T DSP) all have to ramp in 2H, and the record on multi-product new ramps is untested (first PIC revenue only in Q1). FY28 0.66-0.62 ($1.26B) and FY29 0.62-0.66 ($1.44B): exit run-rate held roughly flat as a share of capex while optics peers (LITE, COHR, MRVL post-Lumentum) compete. Other builds: management's >$600M (+$45M FY27); each of three lines >$100M [13] is a floor (~$300M+) = downside.

downside.story: 10th percentile: AI capex follows the standing file's low path (-15% vs base) and Credo loses 1.6T AEC share fast (Marvell/MaxLinear qualified at a top-2 customer, Cisco in-house), copper capture -18%; optics ramp slips (FY27 optical ~$360M, under the >$600M statement); AEC price cuts take 5pt off copper margin; P/E exit ~12.5x.

base.story: Median: AI capex on the standing file's base path; Credo keeps most AEC volume but its capture falls ~25% by FY28 as Marvell/MaxLinear 1.6T AECs and Cisco's in-house program arrive; optics reaches ~$556M in FY27 (below the >$600M statement) and ~$1.26B in FY28; adjusted operating margin ~49-50% FY27-28, 48% FY29; exit 16.5x NTM EPS and 3.0% FCF yield.

upside.story: 90th percentile: capex tracks toward the file's high path, Credo keeps ~90% AEC share through 1.6T (patent position, settlement), optics beats $600M and scales past $1.5B in FY28; FY28 revenue ~$4.6B (above $3.88B consensus); P/E re-rates toward the peer median ~21.5x.

reasoning: Primary-document build. Q1 FY27 (Ex 99.1, 10-Q): revenue $479.0M, non-GAAP op margin 48.2%, cash $764M after the $1.25B DustPhotonics deal ($770M cash, $169M shares, $310M earnout), customers A/B 43%/28%, inventory $313M, $213M supply commitments. Q1 call (speakers named): CFO Daniel Fleming guides Q2 $525-535M, FY27 growth >85%, opex +55%, GM ~flat, ~200M shares; CEO Bill Brennan says >$600M optical in FY27 and 1.6T AEC 'much bigger' in FY28. Guidance record: 7/7 quarterly revenue beats, but the beat fell from +12-20% to +1.6-1.9% in the last two quarters, so we sit at the top of the Q2 range rather than the record-adjusted $596M. Since mid-August the stock fell >50%: AEC competition (Marvell 1.6T AECs at SC26, patent settlement 11-17; MaxLinear's CEO targets 20-30% of 1.6T; Cisco's 1.6T cable quotes), a sector multiple compression (peers down 25-45% in a month; TD Cowen and Stifel cut targets on multiples, not demand), and concentration. Drivers: AI capex from the standing file (base) x a copper capture that falls ~25% by FY28 (share loss) and an optical capture that ramps from ~0.1 to ~0.65 $M per $B. Result: FY27 $2,494M (in line with consensus), FY28 $3,531M (-9% vs $3.88B consensus), FY28 EPS $8.54 (-12%). Valuation: P/E 16.5x (peer median 22.6x shrunk with k=0.8 to CRDO's 15.2x) and a 3.0% FCF yield (departure from the 1.9% default, carded in gap_note: peers' trailing yields embed +50-98% growth that CRDO will not have at the horizon). Downside (P10 $70) moves capex, share, optics, margins and multiple together; upside (P90 $288) is share retained plus optics beat. Research limits: Twelve Data estimates unavailable on this plan; StockAnalysis/MarketBeat pages fetched were cached from 2025 and not used; peer consensus snapshot is 2026-10-23 (flagged). Not driver-linked: none.

Forecast: Q2 FY27 1.40 (copper ~$474M, consistent with inventory up $62M q/q to $313M and $213M non-cancelable supply commitments [1][2]); then ~-4.5%/quarter to 1.09 by Q4 FY28 as (a) 1.6T AEC competition arrives: Marvell demonstrated 800G/1.6T AECs at SC26 [16] and settled its patent challenges with Credo [15]; MaxLinear's CEO Kishore Seendripu (competitor, not a Credo statement) targets 20-30% of 1.6T cables [19]; Cisco sought quotes for a proprietary 1.6T cable program [20]; (b) the CEO Bill Brennan said 1.6T AEC comes in 'in a much bigger way' in FY28 [13], which offsets part of the share loss; then -1%/quarter in FY29 as share settles. Other evidence-based builds: consensus FY28 revenue $3.88B [18] (copper capture held ~1.25 through FY28, +~$0.4B revenue); share held at ~93-99% (no competitor ramp) = upside case; share falling to ~70% in 1.6T = downside case.
drivers.why: The share term carries the AEC competition debate (Marvell, MaxLinear, Cisco in-house) that drove the stock's fall.

drivers.label: Optical capture: optical DSP + ZeroFlap transceivers + SiPho PIC revenue per $B AI capex
drivers.source: CEO/CFO optical statements on the Q1 FY27 call [13][14]; DustPhotonics deal [2][12]
drivers.derivation: Optical revenue is not disclosed. FY26 base estimated at $63M (8/12/18/25 by quarter) and Q1 FY27 $35M (record optical DSP plus first PIC revenue per Bill Brennan, CEO [14]); flag: low confidence, it only splits the reported total. Forecast optical revenue = capture x capex: Q2 FY27 0.18 (~$61M), Q3 0.45 (~$170M), Q4 0.70 (~$291M) = FY27 ~$556M, 7% below the CEO's 'more than $600 million' [13] because three new product lines (ZeroFlap, PICs, 1.6T DSP) all have to ramp in 2H, and the record on multi-product new ramps is untested (first PIC revenue only in Q1). FY28 0.66-0.62 ($1.26B) and FY29 0.62-0.66 ($1.44B): exit run-rate held roughly flat as a share of capex while optics peers (LITE, COHR, MRVL post-Lumentum) compete. Other builds: management's >$600M (+$45M FY27); each of three lines >$100M [13] is a floor (~$300M+) = downside.
drivers.why: The 2H FY27 inflection management describes is optical; it is the largest swing in FY27-28.

drivers.label: Copper/IC segment non-GAAP operating margin
drivers.derivation: Actual quarters: (non-GAAP operating income - estimated optical revenue x 20%) / copper revenue = 0.44, 0.48, 0.51, 0.51, 0.50. Forecast 0.51 in Q2 FY27 (Q2 guide midpoint implies 48.7% total: 530 x 68% - 102.5 opex), 0.53 in 2H FY27 (operating leverage: Daniel Fleming, CFO, guided FY27 non-GAAP opex +55% y/y = ~$420M on >85% revenue growth [13]); 0.52 in FY28 and 0.50 in FY29 as AEC pricing meets Marvell/MaxLinear competition [15][16][19]. Alternative: company-implied ~51% total FY27 operating margin (68% GM - 16.8% opex) = +~1pt.
drivers.why: Margin on the core AEC/IC line; pricing pressure is the second leg of the competition risk.

drivers.label: Optical segment non-GAAP operating margin
drivers.derivation: Actual quarters set at 20% (sub-scale; flag, estimate). Forecast 35% Q2 FY27, 42% Q3, 45% from Q4 FY27: Daniel Fleming (CFO) said FY27 non-GAAP GM stays broadly at FY26's ~68% even with >$600M optics [13], so optics cannot carry a module-maker margin; but ZeroFlap transceivers are modules (optical module peers COHR/LITE run far lower margins), so we hold optics ~5-8pt below copper. Alternative: optics at the copper margin (+~$0.07/share FY28) or at optical-module-peer margins ~25% (-~$0.12).
drivers.why: Mix shift to optics is the main gross-margin risk.

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver set: two segments (Copper and IC; Optical) = AI customer capex x a capture term each, with segment non-GAAP operating margins; adjusted EBIT (ex-SBC) with SBC carried as share dilution (+3.5%/yr). Other income is its own line (3.2% on prior-quarter cash; cash rolls at 30% FCF conversion). Value is carried by the P/E leg (16.5x NTM adjusted EPS at the horizon, 60%) and the tech FCF-yield leg (40%); no DCF, no SOTP (both segments sell into the same AI cluster spend and share one cycle). Driven share of revenue 100%. Year 3 (FY29) is a slowdown year (+9% revenue, 48% margin) as capex flattens in the standing file, close to a mid-cycle exit for growth but still at a high margin; the 16.5x exit and the downside case carry the cyclical risk.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) FCF-yield exit 3.0% vs the default k=0.8 shrink 1.9%: at 1.9% the research target (12m) is ~$225 vs $175 (+29%) -> card. (2) P/E exit on NTM-re-weighted peer EPS (16.5x) vs the run table's printed NTM basis (19.7x, ~+$16 on the blend, ~+9%) -> card. (3) Peer consensus snapshot dated 2026-10-23 is older than the 21-day consensus window (rule 23); peers were re-priced to 2026-11-20 closes and checked against Yahoo FY EPS opened 2026-11-23 [27], which run 5-40% higher for FY2 (so the stale snapshot, if anything, raises the peer median). (4) Optical base and the Copper/Optical split are undisclosed (estimates, low confidence); only the split, not the reported totals, rests on them. (5) CY2025 and CY2029 AI-capex points are outside the standing file's range (CY2029 held at 2028; affects FY29 only). (6) Probable financing: none (net cash $764M, no shelf or ATM found); DustPhotonics earnout is equity-classified $300M [2], in the share drift. fair_value.value = engine base horizon value.
model_inputs.reference_note: consensus FY27 revenue $2.50B, FY28 $3.88B; EPS FY27 $6.31, FY28 $9.71 (Yahoo, 2026-11-23 [18]); our FY27 revenue 2,494 (-0.2%), FY28 3,531 (-9.0%), FY28 adjusted EPS ~$8.5 (-12%): below consensus by more than 5% in FY28 because we take AEC share loss to Marvell/MaxLinear/Cisco and a slower optical ramp.
